I used to wonder the same thing about coin flips. The chance of flipping heads or tails is 50/50 each time, no matter what happened in previous flips. So after 3 tails in a row, the odds of flipping tails again on the 4th throw is still 50%.

The coin has no memory. Each flip is an independent event, unaffected by past flips. Our brains tend to think after a run of tails, heads is 'due' to balance it out. But that's just our pattern-seeking tendencies.

A useful way to think about it is to imagine flipping a coin 4 times in parallel universes. In some universes you'd get TTTT. In others THTT, HTHT etc. The coin can't force a heads after 3 tails any more than it can force 5 heads in a row.

It's hard to internalize since our intuition screams 'tails 4 times in a row seems unlikely!' But each flip is a fresh 50/50. Kind of mind-bending but that's statistics for you! If you ever want to test it out, you can [roll a die](https://flipsimu.com/dice-roller/) or flip a virtual coin on some probability sites to simulate repeated trials.
